Team — circling up after this morning's ops review. I captured a small set of runbook updates + escalation asks that need owners before Friday's Q2 review. Attaching the latest runbook (QBR_runbook_v2.pdf). Please skim and confirm owners below inline.

Quick context: Acme Health is moving toward a pilot that will put predictable throughput and stricter data residency needs on our Private offering. Procurement sent preliminary redlines (copied) and asked for SOC2 evidence. We also have an executive ask for a short slide showing mitigation & SLA commitments.

Action items (high-level) — assign by EOD Wednesday:
- Runbook: finalize failure-mode documentation for Private deployments (owner: TBD).
- Exec slide: 1-slide mitigations + escalation path for QBR (owner: TBD).
- Procurement evidence: provide SOC2 summary + point person for redlines (owner: TBD).
- Roadmap exception: determine whether Private capacity ramp can be accelerated (owner: TBD).

Please reply with your owner assignments and any blockers. If you want me to reassign to someone else on your team, call it out.

Attachments: QBR_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook), Acme_MSA_redlines_20270411.docx (procurement redlines stub)

— Vivek

Quick note on the roadmap exception: we can probably accelerate the Private capacity ramp by re-prioritizing one sprint (roughly 2–3 weeks) but that will require deprioritizing the new Reranking latency work. If the exec ask is to show a mitigation for Acme, I suggest we present a fast-failover flow (single-region private -> hosted fallback) rather than a full capacity commit.

I'll volunteer to own the failure-mode docs (Runbook) with Grace's help. Tentative commit: draft by Thursday EOD; review w/ Vivek Friday morning.

Marissa — can you produce a 1-slide summary (metrics to watch + proposed credit structure) by Thursday EOD and loop in Legal for the residency language? I'll brief execs on Friday if the slide is ready.

Vivek / Lauren — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple requests from our side so we can progress the pilot: 

1) Please provide a SOC2 summary (we'd prefer the most recent report) and a contact for security questions.
2) Data residency: Acme requires EU data not leave EU regions for EU customers — can you confirm options & proposed language?
3) The redlines document has three items we'd like to discuss (liability caps, data deletion SLA, audit rights). We've attached a short spreadsheet that summarizes our asks.

Attachment: SOC2_summary.xlsx (summary stub)

Would prefer a call tomorrow morning (PST) to talk through redlines — proposed 10:00am PST.

— Procurement Team, Acme Health
